# heytownhall_sso_domain_verification (Resource)

Waits until a domain's DNS record is found and the domain is verified. It makes no remote object of its own; it only asks the API to check the record, over and over, until the check passes or the timeout ends. It works like `aws_acm_certificate_validation`.

Use it between the DNS record and whatever needs the verified domain, such as `heytownhall_sso_activation`. If the domain is no longer verified when Terraform refreshes (the record was removed and the API checked again, or the domain was deleted), the resource leaves the state and the next apply verifies again.

Destroying the resource changes nothing remotely.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# aws_route53_record.sso_verify (or a Cloudflare record) publishes heytownhall_sso_domain.acme.verification_record.
resource "heytownhall_sso_domain_verification" "acme" {
  sso_domain_id = heytownhall_sso_domain.acme.id

  timeouts = {
    create = "15m"
  }

  depends_on = [aws_route53_record.sso_verify]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `sso_domain_id` (String) The `id` of the `heytownhall_sso_domain` to verify. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `sso_domain_id`.
- `verified_at` (String) When the API found the record (RFC 3339).

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
